subsystems.name: DID method
subsystems.role: defines one flavour of DID and the rules for creating, resolving, updating and deactivating it.

subsystems.name: DID document
subsystems.role: the machine-readable record a verifier fetches: public keys, verification methods and service endpoints.

subsystems.name: Verifiable data registry
subsystems.role: the shared source of truth that anchors DIDs, replacing a central authority.

subsystems.name: Wallet or agent
subsystems.role: holds the controller's private keys and signs on their behalf.
parts: secure key storage (secure enclave or HSM)

subsystems.name: Credential layer
subsystems.role: the actual statements being proven — a degree, a licence, an employment claim.

subsystems.name: Resolution layer
subsystems.role: turns any DID string into its current document, whatever method it uses.

buildSteps.title: Pick or define a DID method
buildSteps.detail: Choose an existing method such as did:web or did:ion, or write a specification naming the registry, the DID syntax and the operations allowed on it.

buildSteps.title: Generate keys in the wallet
buildSteps.detail: The controller's device or hardware module creates a key pair; the private half never leaves secure storage.

buildSteps.title: Compose the DID document
buildSteps.detail: Public keys, verification methods and service endpoints are assembled into the document the method expects.

buildSteps.title: Anchor it in the registry
buildSteps.detail: The document is published — to a ledger, a batch anchor, or a web domain's well-known path — establishing a root of trust.

buildSteps.title: Resolve the DID
buildSteps.detail: A resolver reads the DID string, routes to the right method driver, fetches and validates the current document.

buildSteps.title: Issue a verifiable credential
buildSteps.detail: An issuer signs a set of claims with its own DID key and hands the credential to the holder's wallet.

buildSteps.title: Present and verify
buildSteps.detail: The holder builds a presentation, optionally disclosing only some fields; the verifier resolves the issuer's DID and checks the signature and status.

buildSteps.title: Rotate, recover and revoke
buildSteps.detail: Keys are rotated or the DID deactivated, and issued credentials are checked against a revocation list so stale ones fail.

prerequisites.why: every DID is just a key pair plus a way to publish the public half; Edwards-curve and elliptic-curve signatures do the work.
a DID needs somewhere to anchor that no single party can silently rewrite — a ledger, or a domain the controller genuinely controls.
self-sovereignty is worthless if the private key can be copied off the device.
W3C DID Core 1.0 became a Recommendation in July 2022, alongside the verifiable-credentials data model, so independent systems can interoperate.
holders need to prove one attribute without revealing the rest, and verifiers need to know a credential has not been withdrawn.

pathway.milestone: W3C-standardised DIDs and verifiable credentials in enterprise and wallet products
pathway.unlocks: credentials that a verifier can check cryptographically instead of phoning the issuer.

pathway.milestone: national and regional digital identity wallets built on these standards, such as the EU Digital Identity Wallet programme under eIDAS 2.0
pathway.unlocks: government-issued identity that citizens hold themselves and reuse across borders.

pathway.milestone: cross-method interoperability, so a wallet holding any DID can present to any verifier
pathway.unlocks: networks where issuers and verifiers never need a shared platform.

pathway.milestone: DIDs built into browsers and operating systems as an ordinary login
pathway.unlocks: sign-in without passwords or per-site accounts, with the user holding the keys.
